correctness.rationale: The non-presheaf conclusion is correct. For a nonempty model, the intervals \(I(a)=(a,f(a))\) with \(a<f(a)\) are proper involution-closed dense-no-endpoint submodels, directed by enlargement, and their union is the whole model. Finite presentability would force the identity to factor through one proper stage, impossible. Thus there are no nonempty finitely presentable models. The fixed-point and fixed-point-free countable examples are non-isomorphic, so the classifying topos has at least two Set-points and cannot be the presheaf topos on the resulting empty/trivial finitely-presentable-model category.
